transcript.text: I can help with that. 'Not working properly' could mean a zone isn't heating, the controls are unresponsive, or something else. The most common simple cause is the child lock being engaged, which disables the controls to prevent accidental use. Could you check if there's a key or padlock symbol lit up on the panel? Also, please tell me if it's a smooth ceramic glass top or one with raised metal rings/coils, as this changes how we diagnose it.
its a smooth glass top one. I don't see a key or padlock lit up. Just the rear right ring isn't heating up, the other three are fine

Thanks for clarifying. Since only the rear right zone is affected and the others work fine, we need to distinguish between a simple compatibility issue and a component failure. Many smooth-top hobs are induction, which won't heat standard pans; if it's induction, try a pan you know works on another zone. If that pan doesn't heat up there either (but does elsewhere), or if you see an 'i' symbol by that ring, it points to the hob itself—either the element/coil or its control module. Please let me know what happens with the test pan and whether you spot any induction markings.
not sure if its induction, its a Zanussi and the manual says ZHRN something. the rear right ring doesn't glow red at all though, even when the display shows a number for it

Since it is a smooth glass top and the rear right ring does not glow red at all (unlike induction which stays cool but heats the pan), this suggests it uses a traditional radiant heating element underneath the glass. Because the other three zones work perfectly, the main power supply to the hob is fine, so the issue is isolated to that specific zone's component or its control switch. The most likely cause is that the radiant heating element itself has failed (burnt out). Less commonly, it could be a loose wire connection or a faulty electronic control module for that zone. As this involves internal electrical components and removing the glass surface, I recommend contacting an engineer to check the element or check the connections safely.

candidates: Child lock or control setting active (high)
Faulty heating element (ceramic/solid plate) or power module (induction) (medium)
